hypotheses.justification: The statement is still true without it; the proof must change. The current proof uses it only through the exact closed form `integral_norm_complexPlaceMellinGaussian` (via `integral_complexPlaceMellinGaussian` / `integral_totallyComplexGaussian_eq_absNorm`). Nothing else needs it: `complexPlaceMellinGaussian` (a product over all infinite places of q_w^(2s-1) exp(-2π (w x)^2 q_w^2)) and `summable_idealSet_inverseNormPower` (FundamentalConeSeries.lean, variables only K, [Field K], [NumberField K]) are general. Proof without it, with σ = Re s > 1, x nonzero in the ideal set, N = |N(x)| ≥ 1, n = [K:ℚ]: (1) by `norm_complexPlaceMellinGaussian` (proved before the IsTotallyComplex variable) the norm is the same product with s replaced by σ. Each 1-D factor integrates to Γ(σ)/2 · (2π (w x)^2)^(-σ), whether w is real or complex, so the summand is C_σ ∏_w (w x)^(-2σ). (2) The ideal set lies in Mathlib's `fundamentalCone`, defined by `logMap x ∈ ZSpan.fundamentalDomain`, which is bounded (`ZSpan.fundamentalDomain_isBounded`). With `logMap_apply` (mult w * (log(w x) - log N / n)) this gives log(w x) ≥ log N/n − C for w ≠ w₀. The product formula N = ∏ (w x)^(mult w) gives the same kind of bound at w₀. (3) Hence ∏_w (w x)^(-2σ) ≤ C' N^(-2σ r/n) with r = number of infinite places. Since 2r ≥ r₁ + 2r₂ = n and N ≥ 1, this is ≤ C' N^(-σ). (4) Conclude by comparison with `summable_idealSet_inverseNormPower K J hs`. Degenerate cases: elements are nonzero (`idealSetElement_ne_zero`), so the Gaussian rates are positive and every integrand is integrable for σ > 0 (no junk values). Totally real and mixed signatures are covered by 2r ≥ n.
